title: NAND is Universal: One Gate Builds Them All
topic: NAND universality — NOT, AND, and every Boolean function can be built from NAND gates alone; tying inputs together makes a NOT, chaining a NAND into a NOT makes an AND, signals propagate through the cascade with the truth table updating in real time

beats.narration: Of all the gates, just one is enough to build every digital circuit you'll ever see — which one, and why?

elements.content: One gate to build them all — but which?

beats.narration: The NAND gate. Output is one — except when both inputs are one, in which case it drops to zero.

elements.content: NAND gate symbol — AND body with output bubble
Input pin labels A, B and output pin Y
all ones — until both inputs are one

beats.narration: Tie both inputs together. Now A NAND A is the same as not A — and just like that, you have an inverter.

elements.content: NAND with both inputs shorted to a single A wire
A signal toggling 0 → 1 → 0 → 1 with Y inverting in sync
A · A = A → Y = NOT A
one gate, a wire — that's a NOT

beats.narration: Feed a NAND into a NOT — also built from a NAND — and the two negations cancel. The result is plain AND. Watch the inputs cycle through every combination.

elements.content: First NAND on A,B feeds a second NAND with shorted inputs (the inverter)
Animated A, B inputs cycling 00, 01, 10, 11 every ~2 s
Live truth table — row matching the current (A, B) glows
NOT (A NAND B) = A AND B
two NANDs in series — AND falls out

beats.narration: OR follows by De Morgan, and from NOT, AND, and OR you can build any Boolean expression. NAND on its own is functionally complete.

elements.content: A + B = NOT (NOT A · NOT B)
NOT, AND, OR — every Boolean function — from NAND alone.
(it's why a single transistor cell can build a whole CPU)
